title: Phased deploy: escape hatches & client-affinity notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal runbook for phased releases where we need to preserve client affinity (sticky sessions) and have multiple fast escape hatches. Mostly a playground for mechanics and edge-case handling; keep lightweight.

High level goals:
- Roll out a new model version or runtime change to a fraction of traffic while keeping long-lived client sessions routed consistently to the same variant (client-affinity).
- Provide 3 fast escape hatches: soft-fallback, immediate pin restore, and emergency circuit-breaker (global).
- Preserve metrics continuity so quality/regression detection is not noisy.

Definitions / terms in this doc:
- cohort: a group of clients / API keys chosen for phased exposure.
- affinity key: value used to keep a client routed to the same backend (client-id, account-id, hashed api-key).
- pin: force route to a specific model version (via console API).
- soft-fallback: automatic downgrade to a cheaper/older model on transient errors.

Affinity design notes:
- Use account_id when available; fall back to first 8 chars of api_key hashed. Avoid IP-based affinity (proxies/multiple devices).
- Affinity cookie/session should be writable by edge layer with TTL 30d for long-lived clients; for short-lived we keep ephemeral affinity in KV for 6h.
- Map: affinity_key -> (route_id, model_version, cohort_id). Store immutably for the life of a session to keep evaluation signal clean.
- If client hits multiple devices (different affinity keys), treat each as separate session for rollout buckets.

Cohort selection checklist (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm cohort size target and distribution (e.g., 1% global or 5% of active web clients).
- [ ] Export list of top 50 customers by traffic and mark as opt-out for early cohorts unless they volunteered.
- [ ] Create cohort tag in routing system: cohort:phased-2026-02-pnb.
- [ ] Sanity-check: verify client IDs map consistently to affinity key (run sample hash over 1000 clients).

Instrumentation & dashboards (must be green before start):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 per cohort and global.
- Error rate (5xx, 4xx) per cohort.
- Model-quality signals: hallucination rate (eval heuristics), token-rejection rate, average length.
- Cost delta: per-token cost vs baseline.
- Alerting: pager if p95 > baseline p95 + 150ms OR 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute.

Rollout sequence (iterative):
1) Canary smoke: 0.1% traffic, 10 min soak. Health: no 5xx, p95 within +50ms.
2) Short soak: 1% traffic, 1 hour. Validate quality signals + manual review of sample responses.
3) Early cohort expansion: 5% traffic, 24h. Have A/B eval set running against expected prompts.
4) Gradual open: step to 20% then 50% with 12–24h between steps depending on telemetry.

Escape hatches (ordered by severity):
- Soft-fallback (fast, local): edge runtime routes a request to fallback variant when model returns error or internal latency > SLO. Implemented in the routing policy with a 200ms cutoff.
  - Pros: automated, minimal operator action.
  - Cons: hides regressions if used too often; must be logged and count as regression signal.
- Pin restore (operator action, targeted): restore a pinned route for a cohort or route_id. API exists: POST /api/v1/routes/:route_id/pin -> { model: X, reason: "rollback" }
  - Typical use: revert cohort back to previous model within seconds.
  - Safety: requires 2FA or elevated token in prod tooling.
- Global circuit (emergency): flip global route-level switch to send all traffic to baseline cluster (fallback region). This is last resort and triggers major incident procedure.
  - Must include announcement stub to customers + disable non-critical autoscaling to prevent cost flares.

Commands / quick actions (examples):
- Pin a route to old model (targeted):
  curl -X POST 'https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/route-234/pin' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PROD_OPS_TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model_version":"text-open-super-2.1","comment":"rollback after p95 spike"}'

- Clear affinity for cohort (rare):
  # careful: will reassign clients to other cohorts; use with small cohorts only
  curl -X POST 'https://internal-api.redwood.ai/affinity/clear' -d '{"cohort":"phased-2026-02-pnb"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'

- Trigger soft-fallback threshold test:
  # simulate slow backend so routing triggers fallback
  curl -X POST 'https://test-inject.redwood.ai/chaos/latency' -d '{"target":"model-2","ms":500}'

Observability notes (practical tips):
- When expanding cohorts, always open a query window for sample responses: 
  SELECT * FROM telemetry.responses WHERE cohort = 'phased-2026-02-pnb' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200
  Save 3 snapshots (after each step) for side-by-side review.
- Keep a pinned notebook with 10 canonical prompts used for quality checks per product vertical.

Open decisions / TODOs: (for followups)
- Decide maximum soft-fallback budget per hour before auto-mitigation: candidate = 0.2% of requests or 1000 fallbacks/hr; needs product approval.
- Should session affinity be sticky across model pin changes? My leaning: yes for a short window (1h) to avoid signal flip, then re-evaluate.
- Need a lightweight UI in Console to show per-cohort affinity map and the last 24h fallback counts. Ticket: JIRA-INF-7821 (linked).

Postmortem / rollback notes template (fill during/after incident):
- Start time / End time / Summary of what happened
- Trigger metric that alerted (exact threshold + value)
- Actions taken (who pinned what and when)
- Root cause hypothesis and verification steps
- Follow-ups and owner

Personal gotchas remembered from past runs:
- If we pin via console but forget to update the routing cache TTL, some edges keep the previous mapping for up to 5m — expect a lag.
- Rolling back regionally without pinning affinity can cause clients to flip variants mid-session; schedule a client notification window if the product cares.
- Do not rely solely on synthetic tests — synthetic can pass while real traffic reveals context-dependent failure.

Contact points during rollout:
- Slack channel: #prod-rollouts (primary monitoring)
- Pager duty: eng-runtime-oncall
- Ops lead: Rafael Ortiz (pager)

Quick logging snippet to paste in incident notes:
- "At 14:12 UTC p95 increased by +220ms for cohort phased-2026-02-pnb. Soft-fallback triggered ~870 reqs/min. Pinned route route-234 back to model text-open-super-2.1 at 14:19 UTC. Steps: pin -> validate sample -> reopen traffic at 14:50 UTC. Root cause suspected kernel selection regression in quantized path. Followup assigned: Rafael."

If nothing else, test the pin flow in staging with a 30s TTL and confirm affinity stickiness before touching prod.

End of notes.

(If I revisit: extract a short checklist card for Console > Releases that product can use.)
